name: Nung (Viet Nam)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read Saul, Janice E. & Nancy F. Wilson. 1980. Nung Grammar (SIL/UTA), phonology ch. 2 in full (via archived sil.org PDF): monosyllabic tonal language, six tones and juncture described, but NO word-stress statement anywhere in the phonology.

tone_statements.citation: Nguyễn Phương Linh & Nguyễn Ngọc Bình. 2025. Hệ thống thanh điệu tiếng Nùng Xuồng (tại thôn Thăm Noọng, xã Tát Ngà, huyện Mèo Vạc, tỉnh Hà Giang) [The tone system of Nùng Xuồng (Thăm Noọng hamlet, Tát Ngà commune, Mèo Vạc district, Hà Giang province)]. Từ điển học & Bách khoa thư 2025(5): 7-13. ISSN 1859-3135.
tone_statements.quote: Trên cơ sở lí thuyết về âm tiết và thanh điệu trong ngôn ngữ học, đặc biệt là cách tiếp cận dựa theo mô hình thi pháp truyền thống (bình - thượng - khứ - nhập), bài viết đã xác định được hệ thống thanh điệu của tiếng Nùng Xuồng bao gồm sáu thanh điệu cơ bản và hai thanh điệu nhập. Kết quả cho thấy hệ thống thanh điệu tiếng Nùng Xuồng có tính khu biệt rõ ràng, được tổ chức theo cặp đối lập cả về âm vực (cao - thấp) và âm điệu (bằng - trắc)
tone_statements.translation: On the theoretical basis of syllable and tone in linguistics, especially the approach based on the traditional prosodic model (bình - thượng - khứ - nhập), the article has established that the tone system of Nùng Xuồng comprises six basic tones and two checked (nhập) tones. The results show that the Nùng Xuồng tone system is clearly distinctive, organised in opposed pairs both in register (high - low) and in contour (level - oblique)
tone_statements.locator: §6 Kết luận, p. 12-13 (also §2 Bảng 1, p. 8: six tones on /a:/)
tone_statements.summary: 6 tones on unchecked syllables + 2 checked-syllable tones ('6+2'), register x contour organisation; acoustic F0 description; TBU = syllable.

tone_statements.citation: 平野綾香 [Hirano, Ayaka]. 2021. ベトナムランソン省チャンディン県のヌン語記述研究 [A descriptive study of the Nung language of Tràng Định district, Lạng Sơn province, Vietnam]. 博士論文 (博士(言語文化学), 甲第21543号), 大阪大学 [Osaka University]. 299 pp. (pdf). doi:10.18910/82267; hdl:11094/82267.
tone_statements.quote: タイ諸語共通でみられる音韻的特徴として声調が挙げられ、ヌン語も声調を有する言語である。チャンディン県のヌン語には以下の(9)に示す 6 種類の声調が存在する。音節末が/p, t, k/で終わる促音節は声調 3 もしくは声調 4 のいずれかの声調をとる。本論では声調を音節末に上付きの数字で示す。 (9) 1：mid-level 2：falling 3：high rising 4：low level 5：low rising 6：glottalized
tone_statements.translation: Tone is a phonological feature common to the Tai languages, and Nung too is a language with tone. The Nung of Tràng Định district has the six tones shown in (9) below. Checked syllables ending in /p, t, k/ take either tone 3 or tone 4. In this study tone is marked by a superscript numeral at the end of the syllable. (9) 1: mid-level, 2: falling, 3: high rising, 4: low level, 5: low rising, 6: glottalized
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: 6 lexical tones (33, 32, 35, 11, 213, 32ʔ glottalized); checked syllables restricted to tones 3/4; TBU = syllable; monosyllabic tone language, no stress statement.

tone_statements.citation: 平野綾香 [Hirano, Ayaka]. 2020. ベトナムランソン省チャンディン県ヌン語の頭子音の史的変化と声調の関係 / The relationship between the tones and the historical sound changes of initial consonants in Nung of the Trang Dinh district, Lang Son province, Vietnam. 東南アジア学会第102回研究大会 (Japan Society for Southeast Asian Studies, 102nd conference, online, 19 Dec 2020), 自由研究発表, Meeting Room 1; abstract in 報告要旨 (Room 1), p. 2.
tone_statements.quote: 上の(1)〜(5)のように、*b-, *d-, *g-, *ɣ-は声調が*B以外の場合はヌン語チャンディン県方言のp-, t-, k-に、声調が*Bの場合はヌン語チャンディン県方言のpʰ-, tʰ-, kʰ-に対応している。*ɟ–は声調が*B以外の場合はヌン語チャンディン県方言のʨ-に、声調が*Bの場合はs-に対応している。タイ祖語の有声音が無声化する際に声調によって無気音と有気音（*ɟ-は破擦音または摩擦音）に分岐する現象は、ヌン語の全ての方言で見られるわけではない。
tone_statements.translation: As in (1)-(5) above, *b-, *d-, *g-, *ɣ- correspond to Tràng Định Nùng p-, t-, k- when the tone is other than *B, and to Tràng Định Nùng pʰ-, tʰ-, kʰ- when the tone is *B. *ɟ- corresponds to Tràng Định Nùng ʨ- when the tone is other than *B and to s- when the tone is *B. The phenomenon whereby Proto-Tai voiced onsets, on devoicing, split into unaspirated and aspirated (for *ɟ-, affricate or fricative) according to tone is not found in all Nùng dialects.
tone_statements.summary: Presupposes the six-tone system of Hirano 2019/2021 (tones cited by number 2, 4, 6); adds that Proto-Tai *B syllables with old voiced stops surface with aspirated onsets (tone 4), a tone-register-conditioned onset split unique among Nùng dialects examined.

sources.note: Historical statement linking tone category and onset: in Tràng Định Nùng the Proto-Tai voiced onsets *b-, *d-, *ɟ-, *g-, *ɣ- each have two reflexes, and the split is governed by Proto-Tai tone — aspirated pʰ-, tʰ-, kʰ- (and s- < *ɟ-) in syllables of Proto-Tai tone *B, plain p-, t-, k- (ʨ-) under *A, *C, *D; examples with modern tone numbers (*boːB > pʰo4 'husband', *beːA > pe2 'raft', *guːB > kʰu4, *ɣamB > kʰăm4 'night'); Gedney's Western Nung (Hudak 2008) shows no such split, so the phenomenon is specific to the Tràng Định dialect.
